note: Authored reference prompts, not measurements. The engine passes these through unchanged (python/studio.py) and has no opinion about what makes a good prompt — adding one should not mean touching Python. Reconstructed from the AI Studio interface; `chip` and `voices` are checked against the engine by tests/test_studio.py, so a preset naming a column that does not exist fails the suite.

presets.title: Castle in the Clouds
presets.summary: Castlevania-style dual-pulse counterpoint over a non-linear triangle bass, with short-noise metallic hats.
presets.prompt: Gothic 8-bit castle theme with melodic pulse leads, solid walking triangle bassline, metallic noise hi-hats, and rhythmic DMC drums. Sense of mystery and royal intrigue.
hints: The triangle is the bass — it reaches A-0 (27.5 Hz) where the pulses stop at A-1, and it has no volume register to duck.
Metallic hats come from `4m:70` on nes3: the short 93-step register is the only pitched noise this chip has.
Counterpoint across two pulses wants different duties — but not 1 and 3, which are the same waveform inverted.

presets.title: AdLib DOS Odyssey
presets.summary: Six-channel OPL2 piece with tremolo and vibrato depth, saw leads and pads — the Sound Blaster sound.
presets.prompt: Early-nineties PC adventure theme on an AdLib card: saw lead over a warm pad, organ counter-line, bell accents, and a square doubling the melody an octave up. Confident, exploratory, a little wistful.
hints: The OPL2's four waveforms are what it has over the YM2612 — but waves 2 and 3 rectify, so they sound an octave above where they are written.
One algorithm bit, not eight: `alg opl0 0` is FM, `alg opl0 1` is additive. On an additive patch attenuating one operator barely changes the level.
Rhythm mode (register 0xBD) is not implemented — use the dac column for drums.

presets.title: Neon Transit
presets.summary: High-octane Mega Drive industrial FM with stereo chorus panning and a rapid sixteenth bassline.
presets.prompt: Dark synthwave / cyberpunk chase with punchy FM resonant slap bass on fm0, detuned stereo lead, metallic stabs, and a driving sixteenth-note motor. Rain-slick, forward, relentless.
hints: Six FM voices and a drum track are mutually exclusive — the DAC takes channel 6 outright.
Keep the drums under the FM with `vol dac 55`: mastering normalises peak and a drum is nearly all peak.
Three voices inside one octave is one thick sound, not three parts. Bass down, lead up.

presets.title: GTR Attack / Runner
presets.summary: Reference-driven study: aggressive guitar-like attack, role rotation between FM voices, and a modulation into a new key without breaking the motor.
presets.prompt: Give me the attack of an aggressive FM guitar, the forward motion of a high-speed runner stage, the density of sixteenth-note action-game writing, then move the lead to another voice and land in a new key without breaking the mechanical continuity.
hints: A reference names two independent things: timbre and motion. One phrase should not be expected to encode every musical dimension.
Role is musical, channel is hardware. The audible lead can move FM1 to FM3 to FM4 while the motor stays continuous.
A section called BREAKDOWN is not one if its RMS barely moves — check with `--profile`.

presets.title: Sunset Boulevard
presets.summary: Slow FM ballad leaning on electric piano and strings, with the PSG holding high sparkle.
presets.prompt: Warm late-eighties Mega Drive ballad: electric piano chords, a soft FM string pad underneath, a singing lead with slow vibrato, and PSG arpeggios high above. Unhurried, golden, a little sad.
hints: Slow vibrato is `455` — 6 Hz at 40 cents, which is where the corpus median sits across 4,839 measured spans.
Sustain Level is inverted: SL 0 holds, SL 15 dies. A pad set to 15 'so it sustains' decays to silence.
PSG pitch resolution runs out above about C6 — let it do sparkle, not the tune.

presets.title: Bell Tower
presets.summary: Channel 3 special mode holding a fixed inharmonic cluster — the FM side's only route to bells and gongs.
presets.prompt: A slow procession under a great bell: struck metallic clusters ringing over a deep sustained bass, sparse and cavernous, each strike left to decay before the next.
hints: `ch3 special` gives fm2's four operators separate pitches. This chip has no FM noise generator, so it is the only way to a fixed inharmonic cluster.
The supplementary register holds a BASE frequency, not a partial: `mul` multiplies it and the algorithm decides whether the operator is heard at all.
To hear the pitches as written, put the channel on algorithm 7 with every `mul` at 1.

presets.title: Boss Approach
presets.summary: Sweep-driven descent and hardware pitch bends over a relentless triangle pulse.
presets.prompt: Something enormous is coming: descending pulse sirens, a triangle bass hammering eighth notes without pause, white-noise crashes, and no melody to hold on to. Dread rather than excitement.
hints: `nes sweep nes0 3 2 down` is the siren — but a downward sweep re-arms the mute that silences a pulse below about 110 Hz.
The pulses bottom out at A-1 (55 Hz) and past the floor the timer clamps, so a written C-1 sounds 888 cents SHARP rather than low.
`12:80` on nes3 is the long-register crash; `4m:70` is the short metallic one.
